source.paper: W. Zhang, S. Ando, Y.-C. Chen, K. Yoshioka, "ASiM: Modeling and Analyzing Inference Accuracy of SRAM-Based Analog CiM Circuits," IEEE TVLSI 2025
source.versionEvidence: The HTML served at urlUsed references its figure assets under the path prefix 2411.11022v4/

units.top1: top-1 accuracy in percent, printed to 0.01 in the figures
units.adcBits: string keys, ADC precision in bits
units.vppPercent: string keys formatted as in the figure row labels ("0.000" ... "0.200"); random-noise or nonlinearity sigma as a percent of the full compute-bit-line Vpp (Sec. IV-C). This is the value passed to ASiM's rand_noise_sigma / non_linear_sigma.
units.lsbNote: The LSBrms equivalents are printed in the Fig. 9/18 row labels and equal vppPercent/100 * (2^8 - 1). They apply to the 8-bit ADC only.

fig6_bitSerialAdc.checkpoint: W8A8 QAT followed by NAT. Sec. IV-B1: 'Both models are trained with 8b/8b weight/activation QAT, followed by fine-tuning with appropriate noise intensities through NAT.' The training-noise intensities are not stated for Fig. 6. The digital baselines in the column headers are identical to Figs. 7 and 9, which suggests the same checkpoints; this is an inference, not a stated fact.
fig6_bitSerialAdc.conditions: Bit-serial; no analog noise; ADC precision 6-10 bits
fig6_bitSerialAdc.valueOrigin: Raster image of a numeric table (2411.11022v4/Fig_Shmoo_BS.png). This is not an HTML table. Values were transcribed by eye from 2x-upscaled crops; each cell is printed to two decimals. No OCR cross-check was done.
fig6_bitSerialAdc.precision: Exact to the printed 0.01 unless mis-transcribed

fig7_adcByEncoding.checkpoint: Same statement as Fig. 6 (QAT then NAT; intensities not stated for this figure)
fig7_adcByEncoding.conditions: Bit-serial and 2-bit/4-bit activation encoding; no analog noise; ADC precision 8-12 bits. Per Sec. IV-B2, signed activations keep the sign bit bit-serial.
fig7_adcByEncoding.valueOrigin: Raster image of a numeric table (2411.11022v4/Fig_Shmoo_BP.png), transcribed by eye from 2x-upscaled crops
fig7_adcByEncoding.precision: Exact to the printed 0.01 unless mis-transcribed
fig7_adcByEncoding.note: Fig. 7's bit-serial column at 8-10 bits is a separate run from Fig. 6 and differs from it by up to 0.03 pp (e.g. ResNet-18 ImageNet at 8 bits: 65.48 in Fig. 6, 65.51 in Fig. 7). Both are reported as printed.

fig9a_randomNoise.checkpoint: W8A8 NAT. Fig. 9 caption: 'ResNet-18 is trained with 100% and 50%, and ViT-B-32 is trained with 60% and 40% training noise intensities for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, respectively.' These match the repo checkpoints resnet18_cifar10_w8a8_pact_trim_100, resnet18_imagenet_w8a8_pact_trim_50, vitb32_cifar10_w8a8_trim_60 and vitb32_imagenet_w8a8_trim_40 (README.md:146-149).
fig9a_randomNoise.conditions: Random noise only (nonlinearity = 0); fixed 8-bit ADC for every encoding
fig9a_randomNoise.valueOrigin: Raster image of a numeric table (2411.11022v4/Fig_Shmoo_Rand_Noise.png), transcribed by eye from 2x-upscaled crops
fig9a_randomNoise.precision: Exact to the printed 0.01 unless mis-transcribed
fig9a_randomNoise.caveat: The 2-bit and 4-bit columns use an 8-bit ADC, which is below their boundary precision (8+2 and 8+4 bits). They therefore mix ADC quantization loss with noise loss; see the 0.000 row.

fig9b_nonlinearity.checkpoint: Same as fig9a (the caption covers both panels)
fig9b_nonlinearity.conditions: Nonlinearity only (random noise = 0). ASiM scales this term by 1/sqrt(MAC*N+1) (module/asim_conv.py:341). Fixed 8-bit ADC.
fig9b_nonlinearity.valueOrigin: Raster image of a numeric table (2411.11022v4/Fig_Shmoo_Non_Linear.png), transcribed by eye from 2x-upscaled crops
fig9b_nonlinearity.precision: Exact to the printed 0.01 unless mis-transcribed

fig10_noiseByAdc.reason: Line plot embedded as an SVG object (2411.11022v4/Fig_Noise_ADC_Dependence.svg). All glyphs are converted to paths (0 <text> elements) and no numeric table exists in the HTML. Values could only be estimated from curve positions, so they are omitted.

fig3_natTrainingNoise.reason: Plot embedded as an SVG object (2411.11022v4/Fig_NAT.svg) with 0 <text> elements and no numeric table. Omitted. The text states only the selected checkpoints' cost: 'a 2.0% accuracy drop for the CIFAR-10 task and around a 3.0% accuracy drop for the ImageNet task' (Sec. III-D).

fig17_natVsNonNat.reason: Plots embedded as SVG objects (2411.11022v4/Fig_Appendix_NAT_Inference_CIFAR10.svg and ..._ImageNet.svg) with 0 <text> elements and no numeric table. Omitted.

fig18_nonNatRandomNoise.checkpoint: Without NAT (QAT only). Appendix text: 'we simulate the 8b/8b ResNet-18 model on CIFAR-10 using the same experimental configuration as in Fig. 9 (a), except that the weights are obtained without NAT.' The digital baseline printed in the header is 93.42%.
fig18_nonNatRandomNoise.valueOrigin: A numeric shmoo table embedded as an SVG object (2411.11022v4/Fig_Appendix_Baseline_Sim.svg) whose glyphs are paths, so it is not machine-readable text. It was rendered to a 2400 px PNG with macOS qlmanage and transcribed by eye.
fig18_nonNatRandomNoise.precision: Exact to the printed 0.01 unless mis-transcribed

tableI_anchor.conditions: Bit-serial ACiM, 256-row parallelism, 6-bit ADC, 0.5 LSBrms noise, 8b/8b ResNet-18, ImageNet
tableI_anchor.correction: 65.44% is the CSNR-based simulator's prediction, not ASiM's. The header row reads ['', 'CSNR', 'CIMUFAS', 'Saikia', 'NeuroSim'] and the accuracy row reads ['Accuracy', '65.44%', '0.10%', '40.82%', '61.09%']. Table I gives no ASiM value. Sec. III-C uses the table to show that existing simulators disagree. For comparison, ASiM's own bit-serial 6-bit-ADC, noise-free ResNet-18 ImageNet result is 2.00% (Fig. 6). Do not use 65.44% as an ASiM calibration point.

siliconValidation_CRCIM.model: 8b/8b ResNet-18; CONV and Linear layers run on-chip, the rest off-chip (Sec. IV-D does not name the dataset in this passage)
siliconValidation_CRCIM.noiseSetup: The measured LSBrms noise was divided equally between random noise and nonlinearity
siliconValidation_CRCIM.majorityVotingExample: Sec. VI-C: 'by applying 3 times oversampling to majority voting with a boundary level of 3, the 6-bit CR-CIM design recovers accuracy from 72.74% to 90.55%'

textThresholds_SecIVC.simpleTasks_CIFAR10_CNN: 'noise intensity should be kept below 0.15 Vpp(%) (~0.4 LSBrms) to maintain inference accuracy above 90%'; for 4-bit encoding '0.025 Vpp(%) (~0.1 LSBrms)'. The figure axis maps 0.025% to 0.064 LSBrms.
textThresholds_SecIVC.complexTasks_ViT_or_ImageNet: 'with an operational voltage Vpp of 1 V for bit-serial scheme, noise intensity needs to be controlled below 0.5 mV to enable functional classification in silicon' (0.5 mV = 0.050 Vpp%)

spotChecks.selection: 3 values drawn with Python random.Random(seed=329866559).sample over all 323 transcribed values; for each, the source table row was re-cropped with its header and row label and compared
spotChecks.evidence: Fig. 9b (Fig_Shmoo_Non_Linear.png), row 0.000/0.000, column ResNet-18 ImageNet Enc = 4. Consistent with Fig. 7 (same encoding at 8-bit ADC, no noise) = 16.26, and with the Sec. IV-B2 text that 4-bit encoding needs 2 more ADC bits.

Fig. 6 (Fig_Shmoo_BS.png), row ADC Precision 7, column ViT-B-32 CIFAR-10. Consistent with Sec. IV-B1: 'any reduction in ADC precision below the boundary causes inference accuracy to approach random guessing in ViT-B-32' (chance = 10%).

Fig. 18 (Fig_Appendix_Baseline_Sim.svg rendered to PNG), row 0.150/0.383, column Enc = 2. Consistent with the appendix text that the non-NAT shmoo 'shows a sharper decline relative to the NAT-enhanced counterpart' (Fig. 9a NAT value at the same point: 74.51).
